head: claude/mi-266-secret-map-jwt-webapp-password
title: MI-266: land the sanctioned propagation path for the two web-api auth secrets
body:
**Tier-1.** Adds `SECRET_JWT_SIGNING_KEY` + `SECRET_WEBAPP_PASSWORD_SHA256` to the `SECRET_*` map in `system-actions.yml`, plus a restore runbook. Landing the **path** is Tier-1; **using** it is Tier-2 and is not done here.

Engineering lane for MI-266, spawned by manager `session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj`.

---

## What this is

These two keys were in the exact state `TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET` was in, and the map's own comment records the precedent in terms: the operator can put a value in Actions and *there is no sanctioned path to move it to the VM*, because a `set-env` with a blank `env_value` resolves EMPTY and the empty-value guard correctly refuses the run. This PR is that path, and nothing more.

**Nothing is armed, no VM is touched, no secret value appears in this diff, the PR, an issue or a log.**

## ⚠️ The mapping arms nothing — verified, not assumed

The repo is public, so the whole point of the map is that the value never reaches the issue body or the run log. I checked this rather than reasoning by analogy, in two parts:

**1. A mapped-but-unset secret still FAILS the run, loudly.** I transcribed the `set-env` branch (`system-actions.yml:1554-1576`) verbatim and ran it:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| mapped, Actions secret **unset** (what lands today) | `::error::` **REFUSED** — exit 1, `REMOTE_CMD` never built, VM never touched |
| mapped, Actions secret **filled** (after the operator pastes) | proceeds |
| `WEBAPP_PASSWORD_SHA256` mapped, unset | `::error::` **REFUSED** |
| `ALLOWED_EMAIL` unmapped, passed inline | proceeds (correct — it is not a secret) |

So until the operator fills the slot, this changes behaviour not at all. **The guard is unchanged and must stay that way** — a refusal here is the mechanism functioning, not something to weaken so the keys "work" early.

**2. The value cannot reach a log.** It flows `secrets.*` → step env → `env_value` → `REMOTE_CMD` → ssh. `REMOTE_CMD` is never echoed, printed or written to a file anywhere in the workflow (checked every reference), and it is built with `printf %q`. `set_env.sh`'s header states values are never logged or recorded in the audit JSON — only the key, the service, and created-vs-updated.

## `ALLOWED_EMAIL` is NOT a secret, and is deliberately not mapped

It is **already in the clear** at `deploy-candidate.yml:137` (`ALLOWED_EMAIL=ben.baichmankass@gmail.com`). It rides `env_value` normally. Mapping it would imply a secrecy it does not have and would make the operator's ask larger than it is — **they originate two values, not three.**

## Target is `env_file: web-api`, and no allowlist change was needed

`ict-web-api.service` is the consuming unit and loads `/etc/ict-trader/web-api.env`. A `shared` write would also hand both keys to `ict-trader-live.service`, which has no use for them. Both the `web-api` target and `ict-web-api.service` are **already** allowlisted in `scripts/ops/set_env.sh` — verified, and nothing in this PR changes either allowlist.

---

## A finding nobody had measured: the gated surface is FOUR handlers, not two

`require_session` is attached to four route handlers:

| route | file | called by the SPA? |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/bot/db/tables` | `db_explorer.py:258` | **yes** |
| `GET /api/bot/db/table/{name}` | `db_explorer.py:306` | **yes** |
| `GET /api/pnl` | `pnl.py:211` | **no** |
| `GET /api/status` | `status.py:38` | **no** |

I then listed every path the SPA actually requests: it calls **neither** `/api/pnl` nor `/api/status`. So **the operator's picture is correct** — Data Explorer is the only dark SPA tab. The other two are gated-and-uncalled, which is why their darkness went unnoticed. Recorded so it is not rediscovered.

## The SPA half: a form and a localStorage token, **not an auth build**

Measured against `benbaichmankass/ict-trader-dashboard`. Population: all **40** `.svelte`/`.ts`/`.js` files under `webapp/src`; positive control: **5** contain `fetch`. Result: **no login UI, no token store** — #11780's finding confirmed.

⚠️ **My first probe was invalid and the control is what caught it.** I grepped `src/`, which does not exist in that repo, and got zero — *with a zero positive control*, which reads identically to "no auth code found". Pointed at `webapp/src`, the control is non-zero and the finding stands.

It is small because the SPA has exactly **one** network chokepoint — `get<T>()` at `webapp/src/lib/api.ts:126-130` — through which all ~19 REST paths pass. No other `fetch`, no XHR, no axios. And `webapp/src/lib/config.ts` already does localStorage-with-a-Settings-field for the API base URL, so the token-store pattern and a place to put the form both already exist. Work: a token store, one header line, a login form, a 401 handler.

⚠️ **What would flip that answer:** `/ws/market` (`webapp/src/lib/ws.ts:78`) is not gated today. A browser `WebSocket` cannot send an `Authorization` header, so if the read gate widens to it, this becomes a real auth build. Worth knowing before Phase H widens the gate.

## The runbook (`docs/runbooks/restore-webapp-auth.md`) — written, NOT executed

The measurement is the part that is easy to get wrong, so it is the bulk of the doc.

#11780 recorded that an **empty** login body returns **422** from Pydantic *before the handler runs* — a probe that would grade the host healthy while it was broken. Every probe in the runbook sends a well-formed body, and the status ladder is read off `routers/auth.py:30-66`, which checks in a fixed order so the code says how far it got:

| code | proves |
|---|---|
| `422` | **nothing** — never reached the handler |
| `500 auth_unavailable` | `ALLOWED_EMAIL` or `WEBAPP_PASSWORD_SHA256` still missing |
| `403 email_not_allowlisted` | ✅ both present |
| `401 invalid_credentials` | ✅ both present **and** email matched |
| `500` *after* a confirmed `401` | `JWT_SIGNING_KEY` specifically is missing |
| `200` + `access_token` | all three present; auth **mints** |

This yields a **credential-free probe**: a well-formed request with the correct email and a deliberately wrong password returns `401` when two of the three envs are live — so any session can prove that half **without holding a secret**. ⚠️ And a `401` does **not** prove `JWT_SIGNING_KEY` is set (the handler never reaches `issue_token` on a bad password), so that half needs a real `200`.

The runbook keeps three facts separate and says to name which you established: **auth mints** · **the gate accepts and still refuses** (it checks that a no-bearer request still returns `401`, because the fail-closed half is what matters most) · **the tab renders** — the third of which cannot be true until the SPA work ships, so until then the honest report is *"the host is restored; the SPA still cannot reach it."*

## Not touched

`src/web/api/routers/db_explorer.py`'s fail-closed behaviour is **correct** and is unchanged. Before the gate, an unauthenticated `GET /api/bot/db/table/trades` returned real rows over 41 columns against `total: 5589` on a public host. No order path is touched; no order was placed, modified or cancelled.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` → **`PASS 56 · FAIL 1 · SKIP 37`**. The one failure is `pr-landing-guard state=undeclared`, the expected intermediate state on push #1 (the declaration + arming file land on push #2).
- ⚠️ An earlier run read `FAIL 4`. The other three were all `No module named pytest` — a container gap, not real failures. With pytest installed those suites are **144 passed**. Reporting the first number as three real failures would have been wrong.
- Workflow YAML parses; both keys present in the `exec` step env; `SECRET_ALLOWED_EMAIL` asserted **absent**.
- `document-index-guard`: `population=1041 registered=1041` → OK (the new runbook is registered).

## Note for the manager

All four claims in my spawn prompt were **verified true**, re-derived rather than trusted. Two process notes: this session was spawned with **no repo attached** (`/home/user` empty, neither repo in scope) — I had to discover the backend via `list_repos` and `add_repo` before I could read `CLAUDE.md`. And both `add_issue_comment` and `create_pull_request` returned **403** (the documented write-scope boundary, not the transient drop), so the board `▶️ START` went through the `board-post` relay ([posted here](https://github.com/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/issues/11336#issuecomment-5632585697)) and this PR through `pr-opener`.
